Yes—paper [1] directly addresses this setup. It studies grading label-free multi-topic science exams where a student’s responses to several distinct topics are merged into one big paragraph with no segmentation indicating which span answers which question [1]. It builds reference answers per question, encodes them, constructs a semantic similarity graph over the references, and uses a combination of retrieval/graph traversal and assignment so each question is graded against its corresponding reference answer independently [1].

Relatedly, rubric-anchored grading is emphasized as a key design principle for reliable open-ended grading [2] and for auditable “rubric judge” paradigms [5], though neither specifically targets the “one big paragraph covering multiple questions”/network-of-reference-answers structure described in [1] [2,5]. Paper [9] focuses on AI-assisted scoring for short written texts with human-in-the-loop oversight, but it does not describe the reference-answer network/graph retrieval approach [9].
